title: Model Spec Midtraining: Improving How Alignment Training Generalizes
authors: Chloe Li, Nevan Wichers, Sara Price, Samuel Marks, Jon Kutasov (Anthropic)
summary: Model spec midtraining (MSM): training on synthetic documents about the Model Spec after pretraining but before alignment fine-tuning, so models learn 'the right thing for the right reasons,' improving generalization and reducing agentic misalignment.
key_result: MSM+alignment fine-tuning cut agentic misalignment from 68%->5% and 54%->7%, beating deliberative-alignment baselines with ~40x less alignment fine-tuning data.
open_threads: May not scale with high-compute reasoning post-training; harder evals needed.

title: SLEIGHT-Bench: Finding Blind Spots in AI Monitors
authors: Elle Najt, Tyler Tracy, Fabien Roger, Joe Benton (Anthropic)
summary: A benchmark of 40 synthetic evasive transcripts across 11 attack categories designed to exploit blind spots in frontier monitoring systems; monitors systematically fail on attacks exploiting capability gaps like precise counting or tracking cumulative state.
key_result: On Claude Opus 4.6, only 8 of 40 attacks reliably detected at 1% FPR; 50% of attacks never caught across 10 trials.
open_threads: Synthetic transcripts may lack realism; targeted fixes for one blind spot degrade others; ensemble monitors costly.

title: Downstream Connections Predict Which Features Will Steer Model Behavior (Circuits Updates May 2026)
authors: Purvi Goel, Isaac Kauvar, Nicholas L. Turner (Anthropic)
summary: Preliminary interpretability work predicting which features causally steer outputs under intervention; features with similar activations/output preferences behave very differently under steering, and downstream connectivity predicts behavioral relevance better than activation-based characterization.
key_result: Downstream connectivity predicts which features actually steer behavior better than activation/output characterization alone.
open_threads: Explicitly preliminary; generalization across models/layers untested.

title: Project Fetch: Phase two
authors: Michael Ilie, C. Daniel Freeman, Kevin K. Troy (Anthropic Frontier Red Team)
summary: Repeats the Project Fetch robotics evaluation with newer models; Claude Opus 4.7, without human assistance, dramatically outperformed prior models and earlier human teams on robotic manipulation tasks.
key_result: Claude Opus 4.7 ~20x faster than the fastest human team at all previously-completed tasks; four shared tasks in 9m35s vs 181m.
open_threads: Struggled with precise closed-loop control; no low-level actuation eval; reliability of final autonomous fetch unclear.

title: Measuring LLMs' impact on N-day exploits
authors: Winnie Xiao, Nicholas Carlini, Milad Nasr et al. (Anthropic Frontier Red Team)
summary: Evaluates how frontier LLMs accelerate exploit development for publicly disclosed but unpatched vulnerabilities (N-days), testing Claude Mythos Preview against Firefox and Windows kernel bugs.
key_result: Produced eight complete Windows-kernel privilege-escalation exploits in ~12 hours for ~$15,700 — the binding constraint on N-day attacks is now 'a few thousand dollars and API access.'
open_threads: Focused on specific vuln classes; ignores other attack stages; controlled environments; cross-platform effectiveness uncertain.
